critical_code_review_comments: modules/pamm/risk_state.py: consistency-basis design is airtight — two indexed count_documents ({account,status} and {account,status=closed,closed_at>=week0}) give an O(1) fingerprint that changes on ANY trade open/close/delete, so a stale payload cannot be served even if disk contents are tampered. The RISK_STATE_MAX_AGE_S=600s age gate covers in-place mutations that don't move a count (e.g. slippage stamping on an existing trade).

Every helper (ensure_indexes, compute_basis via strategy_guard wrap, read_state, store_state, nav_peak) catches Exception and logs — cache infra can never crash the guard. Verified experimentally in the adversarial test: replacing compute_basis with a RAISE still yields correct evidence.

strategy_guard._telemetry (L426-560): cache_ok flag correctly gates store_state at the recompute path's tail — partial evidence gaps (open-exposure failure or loss-scan failure) set cache_ok=False so a broken read is never persisted. The maintained branch reads slips-median/p95/count in one traversal and preserves consecutive_losses semantics identical to recompute.

nav_peak keyed by pamm_nav_snapshots.count_documents({program_id}) is correct because snapshots are append-only — any new snapshot bumps the count and forces the max-scan. limit(20000) is a safe rescan bound; would recommend documenting this ceiling in the docstring for programs that could exceed it.

iter218+iter220 market_closed skips are correctly implemented — the pytest.skip fires on blocked='market_closed', not on any other reason, so the kill-switch/env-caps remain fully tested even on weekends.
